record.original_question: Let G be a finite group with |G| = n. Consider the n x n matrices A1, ..., An obtained from the regular representation of G. In this group-representation setting, is the Matrix Spencer bound true; namely, is there a universal constant C > 0 such that one can choose signs epsilon1, ..., epsilonn in {+1, -1} with ||sum_{i=1}^n epsiloni Ai|| <= C*sqrt(n)?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2 (Group Spencer). Let G be a finite group of size n. Conjecture 1 holds in the particular case in which A1, . . . , An are the n × n matrices corresponding to the regular representation of G.
In [BKMZ22] we prove Conjecture 2 for simple groups, but the general case is still open.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a finite group of order n, and let {e_g : g ∈ G} denote the standard basis of ℂ^n indexed by elements of G. The (left) regular representation of G assigns to each g ∈ G the n × n permutation matrix A_g defined by A_g · e_h = e_{gh} for all h ∈ G. Enumerate the elements of G as g_1, …, g_n and set A_i := A_{g_i}, so that A_1, …, A_n are n × n {0,1}-matrices, each a permutation matrix.

Question: Does there exist a universal constant C > 0, independent of G and n, such that for every finite group G of order n one can choose signs ε_1, …, ε_n ∈ {+1, −1} satisfying
   ‖ ε_1 A_1 + ε_2 A_2 + ⋯ + ε_n A_n ‖ ≤ C · √n,
where ‖·‖ denotes the spectral (operator) norm?
artifact.status_search_result: The Group Spencer conjecture has been established for finite simple groups (work on the concentration of Gaussian Cayley matrices, e.g. arXiv:2212.00066), but the general case across all finite groups remains open. The broader Matrix Spencer conjecture has been resolved up to poly-logarithmic rank by Bansal–Jiang–Meka, which does not settle the regular-representation case (rank n).

status_evidence.title: On the concentration of Gaussian Cayley matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Studies Gaussian series of matrices in the image of the left regular representation of finite groups, with applications to the matrix Spencer conjecture; establishes results for simple groups.
status_evidence.claim: The Group Spencer conjecture is proved for finite simple groups, but the general case is open.

status_evidence.title: Resolving Matrix Spencer Conjecture Up to Poly-logarithmic Rank
status_evidence.snippet: Bansal, Jiang, and Meka prove the matrix Spencer conjecture for matrices of rank up to n/polylog(n).
status_evidence.claim: General matrix Spencer is settled only up to poly-logarithmic rank, which does not cover the full-rank regular representation case.
